criticalItems: C1 The page wired NO event handlers - every control in the composed page was inert. Clicking a page number or a sort header emitted into the void, and the table kept announcing aria-sort='none' on a control that could never change. Compounding it, CourseFilesPageData had no `sort` field, so the table's model structurally could not carry one and the table's own JSDoc was false as wired. FIXED: added `sort` to the page's data type and three handlers that REPLACE this.data rather than mutate it.

C2 sl-badge private-API reach-past (--_background/--_color), which also silently re-opened a decision the decomposition had closed: the approved tree specified a bespoke <span> precisely BECAUSE sl-badge is borderless, and the code used sl-badge anyway and painted a border on from outside. FIXED: replaced with a bespoke <span>; the run now has ZERO private reach-pasts.

stage1CodeConnectBlock.what: design-analyst returned BLOCKED_ON_CODE_CONNECT; every instance resolves to {}.

stage1CodeConnectBlock.rootCause: The design is drawn against itslearning's OWN component library (instances named Navigation, PageHeader, Banner, Cell, Pagination, Status Tag, Course Hat), not the SL Design System library. This is NOT the subtree-scoping artifact the runbook warns about - per-node calls were made and were also empty.
stage1CodeConnectBlock.whyTheBlockIsWrong: The block's stated remedy is 'publish Code Connect mappings in Figma and re-run'. That remedy cannot apply: the components are not SLDS components, so there is nothing to map them to in this file. The pipeline halts permanently on a class of design it can never unblock.

stage2DecomposerOverran.note: A nudge asking for a partial tree was queued but the agent had stopped calling tools, so the message was never picked up. There is no timeout or liveness check anywhere in the pipeline.

coordinatorRoleUndefined.what: This is the third orchestrator in the batch to end a turn on a status line while stages remained.
coordinatorRoleUndefined.diagnosis: Not an agent defect - a gap in the skill. SKILL.md specifies how to spawn stage agents and how to route work back, but says nothing about what the coordinator does while a child runs, and defines no liveness check, timeout, or give-up rule. The default behaviour of 'spawn and await' therefore reads as a legitimate stopping point.
coordinatorRoleUndefined.suggestedFix: The skill should state that a coordinator keeps working while children run (verifying the previous stage's output, pre-resolving tokens, staging the next brief), and should define a per-stage timeout after which the coordinator proceeds without the child and records it.

stage2CoordinatorRaceCondition.what: The coordinator wrongly concluded the decomposer had stalled, authored a parallel decomposition, and dispatched two implementers before the real answer arrived 434s in.
stage2CoordinatorRaceCondition.consequence: Two trees existed briefly. The decomposer's is better evidenced (it read paginator/inline-message/badge/tag/avatar/select/search-field/text-field/link/grid sources) and was adopted. One coordinator decision was NOT reverted - the nav stayed as one component instead of the decomposer's two - because its implementer was already running.
stage2CoordinatorRaceCondition.rootCause: The pipeline has no liveness signal and no expected-duration guidance for a stage agent. 434s of silence is indistinguishable from a hang. My earlier finding 'coordinatorRoleUndefined' said the skill does not say what a coordinator does while a child runs; this is the same gap producing the opposite error - not idling, but acting too early.
stage2CoordinatorRaceCondition.correctionApplied: The decomposer specified the selected page fill as --sl-color-palette-purple-800 (#42354a), read from a stale pre-measurement section of the manifest. The measured pixel is #5d4a68 = --sl-color-palette-purple-700. Corrected in the manifest and in the pagination-bar implementer's brief before any code was written.

inventedTokenSurvivedToImplementation.what: The coordinator asserted this token in the manifest Token Reference and in three implementer briefs. IT DOES NOT EXIST in any theme in the repo.
inventedTokenSurvivedToImplementation.whyItMatters: An undefined custom property in a var() with no fallback makes the browser DROP THE WHOLE DECLARATION. tsc cannot see it, the Stage 3 gate cannot see it, and the page renders unstyled while every check passes. A white-on-white surface would have looked plausible in a capture.
inventedTokenSurvivedToImplementation.caughtBy: Both leaf implementers independently, by grepping the theme before using it. Neither accepted the brief at face value.
inventedTokenSurvivedToImplementation.pipelineGap: There is NO stage in the pipeline that verifies a referenced --sl-* token exists. The coordinator wrote one (scratchpad/tokencheck.mjs) and ran it over the generated tree; it should be a real Stage 3 gate alongside the type check.
inventedTokenSurvivedToImplementation.inconsistencyItRevealed: The two implementers chose DIFFERENT replacements for white - top-nav used --sl-color-white, course-table used --sl-elevation-surface-raised-default. Both resolve to #ffffff so both are correct, but the run now uses two token names for one colour. A shared brief that names the right token prevents this; mine named a wrong one.

recurringTS4114.what: `static get scopedElements()` on a ScopedElementsMixin host requires an `override` modifier under this tsconfig. The generated root hit TS4114.
recurringTS4114.generalises: YES - the sibling run b-itsl-bookmk-deleted-course has the IDENTICAL error on the identical member, surfaced by typecheck.mjs's new errorsInOtherRuns bucket. Two independent runs produced the same defect, so it is a gap in the framework skill's ScopedElementsMixin example, not a one-off slip.
recurringTS4114.suggestedFix: The Lit framework skill's ScopedElementsMixin snippet should show `static override get scopedElements()`.

lintersCannotRun.what: Neither linter runs in this checkout. `npx eslint` fails with Cannot find package 'eslint-plugin-lit' (imported by tools/eslint-plugin-slds); `npx stylelint` fails with Could not find 'stylelint-config-standard'.
lintersCannotRun.impact: The pipeline has no lint gate in practice. The repo's own slds/button-has-label rule never ran over any generated file - and the reviewer's M12 (a focusable search button sharing its accessible name with the input) is exactly what that rule exists to catch. Pre-existing dependency gap, not caused by this run, but it means a stated quality control is absent batch-wide.

criticalFoundOnlyByReview.what: C1 - the entire page was non-interactive - passed every automated gate.
criticalFoundOnlyByReview.why: tsc is clean (handlers are optional), the token check is clean, and the Stage 4 capture is a STILL IMAGE, so a dead button is indistinguishable from a live one. Only a human-style code review caught it.
criticalFoundOnlyByReview.implication: Stage 4 as defined measures appearance only. A design implemented as a photograph of itself scores identically to a working one. If the pipeline is to certify more than looks, Stage 4 needs at least one interaction assertion per emitted event.

NOT fixable through the public API; itemLabel can only be emptied, not the separator changed.
slds-component-viability.gridViable: sl-grid + sl-grid-column(width=280, renderer) + sl-grid-sort-column can produce the 4x280 layout with two sortable headers.

There is NO public API for border width - matching the design requires setting the PRIVATE --_border-width (or --_border-color) custom property from outside. This is the 'reaching past the public API' case.

stage4Discrepancies: BANNER, three ways, all from composing the real `sl-inline-message` and all left unfixed deliberately: (1) background is --sl-color-background-info-subtlest = #0055b01a, compositing over white to ~#e5edf7, where the design is #ecf8ff; (2) it draws a 2px border in --sl-color-border-info-bold (#0f3b73) and the design has NO border; (3) it is 60px tall against the design's 45px, which pushes everything below it down 15px. Fixing any of these means overriding the component's private --_background or nulling its border from outside. Not done: the measurement is the point.
BANNER TEXT COLOUR: sl-inline-message renders its body in --sl-color-foreground-info-bold (navy); the design's banner text is #333333.

The design's `arrow-up-arrow-down` sort glyph is not registered; the theme's `sort` is used. The design's `magnifying-glass` is not registered; the theme's `search` is used. All three are the same idea in a slightly different drawing.

COURSE HAT COLOURS UNBOUND: the design's #d9e3e8 fill and #72838d glyph have NO token in the itslearning theme. The badge uses --sl-color-palette-grey-200 instead, so it reads grey where the design reads blue-grey.
